pr_title: EVP: Don't find standard EVP_PKEY_METHODs automatically
pr_body:
EVP_PKEY_meth_find() got called automatically any time a new
EVP_PKEY_CTX allocator was called with some sort of key type data.
Since we have now moved all our standard algorithms to our providers,
this is no longer necessary.

We do retain looking up EVP_PKEY_METHODs that are added by the calling
application.

Fixes #11424
pr_comments:
> No, not that simple, unfortunately.

The fact that it uncovers bugs (which is what it does) is, well, unfortunate, but I'll maintain that the solution itself is simple.
It also breaks gost-engine tests. So could you please add the extended tests to this PR if they are compatible with current CI?
~I haven't the faintest idea why it would break the GOST engine...~ ... or maybe I do.  When a bug fix contains a bug, all hell breaks loose :wink:

~I found a case when this breaks...  anytime someone calls `EVP_PKEY_assign()` or one of its wrapper macros.  I had forgotten about those, and those calls are also the time when we do fall back on EVP_PKEY_METHODs.~

~Closing this.~

Actually, it's too late at night to make that decision.  I'll get back on this tomorrow.

Being a little more awake now, I found that there's an oddity in `test/ectest.c` : `custom_params_test()`, where the keys with custom groups are unexportable (i.e., `evp_pkey_export_to_provider()`, which gets called by `EVP_PKEY_derive_init()`, fails, which means that `EVP_PKEY_derive_init()` jumps to the legacy section...  which needs a non-NULL `ctx->pmeth` to do its work.

The section of code that causes the export to fail is this:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0c3eb2793b2a1fe35beeb90ba8f5cb2a0fdc3270/crypto/ec/ec_lib.c#L1698-L1714

The failure is caused by `encoding_flag == OPENSSL_EC_NAMED_CURVE`

...  and this is where I don't quite understand the ins and outs of the EC code, and would like some help figuring out this failure.  I thought that at this point, keys with custom groups could be handled by the provider, but maybe I misunderstood...  @romen?  @slontis?

You don't need this PR to get the export failure, it happens in master as well.  You only need a breakpoint here [*] to see it in action:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0c3eb2793b2a1fe35beeb90ba8f5cb2a0fdc3270/crypto/evp/exchange.c#L226

[*] well, apart from the obvious breakpoint at `custom_params_test`, of course...
I was looking at `asn1_flag` with quite a bit of suspicion, but didn't dare look too deeply.  Thanks for uncovering/confirming!  I'll apply your patch.

> GOST tests are OK.

Cool.  So, final review?
This pull request is ready to merge

Merged

issue_context.title: Falling back to legacy when we shouldn't
issue_context.body:
In some internal tests I just saw a TLS connection successfully perform an X25519 operation in a library context which only had the FIPS provider loaded - not the default provider. This is unexpected because X25519 does not exist in the FIPS provider (yet).

The reason seems to be because in our key exchange code we attempt to fetch the algorithm from the available providers. However if that does not work we fallback to legacy and see if the legacy path can help us. And of course in this case it can.

This is undesirable because if you only have the FIPS provider loaded you only want FIPS crypto being performed. Anything else should fail.

We should only really fallback to legacy if we know that an engine can service the request.

My guess is this same issue applies to other operations besides key exchange.
comments:
Yup.  However, we're still in an interim state when *everything* hasn't moved to providers (I'm still working on complete RSA-PSS support in a local branch, for example, and there's SM2 as well).  It's much to early at this time to turn off that fallback.

BTW, turning off the fallback is fairly simple...  it should enough to empty this array:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/9e2c03582de42e8ac5aa23412affcb9645395e94/crypto/evp/pmeth_lib.c#L39-L85

... and possibly this array:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/9e2c03582de42e8ac5aa23412affcb9645395e94/crypto/asn1/standard_methods.h#L15-L60

... although I suspect that emptying that array comes with consequences.
Can we empty the arrays where we *have* completed the conversion (which is most of them)? Just leave the ones which are incomplete?
@levitte Hello, what do you think about turning off the fallback now?

I could see dropping the array of "standard" `EVP_PKEY_METHOD`s.  Regarding `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD`, I'm a little more dubious, as they serve to export legacy EVP_PKEYs to provider EVP_PKEYs, among others...
Actually, it's even easier than I imagined.  PR coming up!
